question: Let $A = \begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}$, and $|A| = 1$. Find $\operatorname{adj}A$ and verify that $A(\operatorname{adj}A) = I$.
explanation:
$|A|=ad-bc=1$.
$\operatorname{adj}A = \begin{bmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{bmatrix}$
$A\operatorname{adj}A = \begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{bmatrix}$
$= \begin{bmatrix} ad-bc & -ab+ba \\ cd-dc & -cb+da \end{bmatrix}$
$= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = I$
Therefore, $A(\operatorname{adj}A) = |A|I = I$.
